name: Enfamil Family Beginnings
whatYouGet: Advertised as up to $400 in free gifts: you may be eligible for free formula samples, discount checks, cash-back rebates, Belly Badges, app access and weekly tips. Joining also enters you in a quarterly drawing for a year of free formula.
costDetail: Free to join; no purchase necessary for the sweepstakes
eligibility: Sweepstakes entry is for legal US residents 18+ who join in 2026; benefits vary by the details you give
catches: Samples are 'may be eligible', not guaranteed; benefits vary by family. Joining agrees to receive offers and communications from Enfamil and affiliated Reckitt brands. Sweepstakes promotion ends Dec 31, 2026.
notes: Quick form asks first and last name, email and due or birth date. Enfamil Rewards points (100 for joining, 1,000 for first app login) are part of the same sign-up.

name: MyGerber Baby account (formula sample opt-in)
whatYouGet: Free MyGerber account with perks such as expert advice and order tracking; sign-up includes an optional checkbox to receive infant formula samples and offers if they become available.
costDetail: Creating an account is free
eligibility: Parents with a child's birthday or due date
catches: Samples are only 'if they become available' and an address is required only if you tick the sample box. Gerber also markets a new-member sample box, but no published schedule or sample eligibility was found. Good Start formula has moved to Perrigo, so the current sample offer is unconfirmed.
notes: gerber.com blocks automated reading, so details come from gerber.com search results only and may be incomplete. On 2026-11-10 the sign-up link was moved to the "Join MyGerber Membership" page on www.gerber.com because the older register.gerber.com address did not resolve in our link check.

name: MySimilac Rewards
whatYouGet: Formula coupons, points toward a bonus coupon, nutrition guidance and partner perks. The welcome kit may include formula samples.
costDetail: Free to join
eligibility: Legal residents of the 50 states and DC, 18+; enrollment is per eligible child up to 9 months; one account per household per child
catches: Samples are not guaranteed ('may'). The Shutterfly free photo book shown on the page carried an offer expiry of July 31, 2026, so it is not listed. Optional SMS opt-in; email and postal marketing continue even if you decline texts. Points are earned only when a coupon is redeemed (5 points each); a special coupon comes at 35 points. Some offers may need a visit to a participating healthcare facility. Program can change or end at any time.
notes: Registration asks for name, home address, email and baby's birth or due date, plus a password. Coupons may arrive by mail, in your account or by email.

name: Nutramigen Support Program (within Enfamil Family Beginnings)
whatYouGet: Specialized track within Enfamil Family Beginnings for families managing cow's milk allergy: emails with articles and expert tips on cow's milk protein allergy, plus free samples and offers (the form says 'tips and samples to fit your needs'). Members also get an entry in the free-formula-for-a-year sweepstakes.
costDetail: Free to join
eligibility: Families managing cow's milk allergy; also joins you to Enfamil Family Beginnings
catches: Sample contents and timing are not specified on the page; some gifts may arrive closer to your due date. Form includes an optional mobile number for text messages. Agrees to receive offers from Mead Johnson affiliated companies and shares your information with them.
notes: Form asks name, email, address, due or birth date and relationship to baby. Talk to your pediatrician before choosing a hypoallergenic formula. Page no longer mentions insurance support.

name: Baby Registry Welcome Box
whatYouGet: Free gift box with sample and full-size items for parents and baby, for Prime members with a baby registry.
costDetail: Requires an active Prime account, a registry with 10 unique items, and over $10 of purchases from the registry (by you or others).
eligibility: Primary registry owner with an active Prime account; Amazon Business accounts do not qualify.
catches: Amazon's help page (read via domain search snippet; the page itself did not fetch cleanly) says tax, shipping, Prime and gift card purchases don't count toward the $10, the box shows $35 until a $35 promotional balance is applied, it ships to the contiguous US only, and a new box needs an 8-month wait. Limited-time and subject to change.
notes: The same registry page also advertises a 15% completion discount, up to $300 in savings, and free 1-year returns. Older Q&A mentions a 60% checklist rule; the current page says 10 items.

name: Baby Registry Welcome Box
whatYouGet: Baby Box with at least six sample-size baby or parenting products plus discount coupons; contents vary.
costDetail: Free box. Registry created on or after 2/1/25, open 7+ days, 20+ unique items, and over $25 purchased through your registry link (items marked Purchased don't count).
eligibility: Adults 18+ in the 50 US states and Puerto Rico; one box per person, Walmart account and household per 365 days.
catches: While supplies last, first come first served; not guaranteed even after meeting requirements and Walmart need not notify you if supplies run out; contents may be substituted; allow 10-12 weeks by US mail to the registry address (no P.O. boxes).
notes: Claim via the banner on your registry page; you get a confirmation email. Support: support@walmartbabywelcomebox.com. The page shows no separate free postpartum or mom box.

name: Free cleaning service with baby registry
whatYouGet: One free home cleaning (1 bedroom, 1 bathroom, kitchen and common areas in a single home, a $99 value) from a partner service provider.
costDetail: Registry open 7+ days with 20+ unique items and $300 spent on items from the registry (by you or invited gifters).
eligibility: Adults 18+ in the 48 contiguous states; limit one per person. Registry must be created on or after the reward start date (Feb 9, 2026).
catches: Available while supplies last; fulfilled by an unaffiliated service provider with its own terms; must redeem no later than 90 days after your registry event date; merchandise total excludes taxes, shipping and fees, and items marked purchased don't count.
notes: Walmart calls this a Tier 2 registry reward alongside the Baby Box.

name: Hello Baby Box
whatYouGet: Free welcome box of product samples and partner offers (diapers/wipes, bottles, skincare, coupons); contents vary.
costDetail: Add 3 items from other stores, complete 40% of the registry checklist, make a $30+ Babylist Shop purchase (a gifter may), and pay $8.95 plus tax shipping.
eligibility: Arrival date under 9 months away or baby under 4 weeks old; one box per household and per registry; US addresses.
catches: Shipping fee is non-refundable and orders can't be changed; AK/HI total shipping $18.95; gift cards and return credit can't pay the fee; Babylist Health and other retailer orders don't count toward the $30.
notes: Babylist's help center blocks automated reading, so these terms come from official-domain search results and may be incomplete. Babylist's marketing FAQ says one box per household per year; the help center says per household and per registry. The sign-up link opens Babylist's "Create a Baby Registry" page because a registry is needed first; the help center says to claim the box from the For You tile on your registry dashboard or in the app. The older /hello-baby/box address only redirects to the help center.

name: MacroBaby Gift Box
whatYouGet: Free welcome box of baby samples, coupons and products from trusted brands, est. value $80+; contents are random and seasonal. Added to your shipment after your first qualifying registry purchase.
costDetail: Add at least 20 items to a registry and make a first qualifying purchase of $15 or more from it.
eligibility: One box per qualifying registry.
catches: Contents can't be requested; if the qualifying items are returned the box must be returned or an $80 fee applies; program can change or end without notice.
notes: Gift box page confirmed directly: add at least 20 items to your registry and make a first qualifying purchase of $15.00 or more from it. The Baby Registry page also advertises 5% cash back on registry purchases.

name: Registry welcome bag
whatYouGet: Goody bag with free samples, coupons and a Registry Guide.
costDetail: Free with registry; available for pickup in stores only.
eligibility: Baby registrants; details of eligibility not confirmed.
catches: Pickup in stores only; ask for the bag when registering in person per store pages. Eligibility and any purchase conditions were not stated in the results.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. buybuy BABY pages refused or failed to fetch; store-page search snippets still describe a free goody bag with samples, coupons and a registry guide. Snippets also mention a 15% completion discount and free first-year shipping after $1,500 of registry gifts.

name: Registry Welcome Kit (Target Baby Box)
whatYouGet: Welcome kit valued at $100, a mix of samples and a Target Circle Bonus.
costDetail: Free kit, but shipping and handling fees apply. Needs a free Target Circle account (Target says Circle is free to join), a baby registry with 10 unique items, and a purchase over $10 from the registry (by you or others).
eligibility: Active baby registries created after 08/15/2023 that haven't claimed a previous kit; one kit per year.
catches: Online only, as a Target Circle Bonus that must be accepted; shipping and handling fees apply; limit one kit per year; registries that claimed a previous kit aren't eligible. Allow 24-48 hours for the bonus to be issued.
notes: Active registries created after 08/15/2023 are eligible. The bonus shows on the registry dashboard. Target's registry sign-up page and product page did not mention the kit in readable text, so only the help article confirms it.

name: MAM Club
whatYouGet: 10% welcome voucher and 10% member discount on the MAM US online shop, plus a pregnancy newsletter, invitations to product tests and prize giveaways.
costDetail: Free to join; discounts apply to purchases in the MAM online shop
eligibility: Not stated; open to anyone registering on the MAM US shop
catches: Main perks are discounts on MAM shop orders (a coupon, not a free item); product tests and giveaways are not guaranteed. Regular newsletter emails.
notes: Registration form was not opened, so exact fields are unconfirmed. Welcome voucher terms were not shown on the club page.

name: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library
brand: Dolly Parton's Imagination Library (The Dollywood Foundation)
whatYouGet: A high-quality, age-appropriate book mailed each month to registered children at no cost to the family.
costDetail: Books are 100% free to enrolled children; local program partners cover book and shipping costs.
eligibility: Children (the US page refers to ages 0-5) living in an area covered by a local program partner; the check-availability page lets you register online or by mail where offered.
catches: Only available where a local program partner serves your address. One local program reported 8-10 weeks for the first book.
notes: Check availability by location first. The search-result snippet about 8-10 weeks came from a local program page.

name: Huggies Rewards
whatYouGet: Free rewards program and app where purchases of Huggies products earn points that can be redeemed for rewards such as gift cards.
costDetail: Free to join; earning points requires buying Huggies products.
catches: Points require buying Huggies products. Search snippets disagree on the sign-up bonus amount, so none is listed. Older Rewards+ (Fetch) earning ended per a Huggies page. Huggies pages disagree on whether the program runs in the Huggies app or as Huggies Rewards+ inside the Fetch app; check the app page before you buy anything for points.
notes: huggies.com blocks automated reading, so details come from huggies.com search results only and may be incomplete. On 2026-11-10 the sign-up link was moved to the Rewards app page on www.huggies.com, and an older www1.huggies.com source page was removed because that host no longer resolves.

name: P&G brandSAVER Points & Rewards
whatYouGet: Free to join. Earn points by completing a profile, taking surveys or scanning receipts for P&G products, then redeem 750 points for a $5 off any P&G product digital reward or use points for sweepstakes entries. Also offers coupons and rebates on 60+ P&G brands.
costDetail: No cost to join, or any fees ever (per the site)
catches: Privacy policy says P&G discloses personal data to third-party partners where it has a lawful basis, receives data from other companies, and may share hashed email identifiers with ad platforms (Google, Meta, Microsoft, Pinterest, Reddit, Snap, TikTok) for interest-based ads. Its FAQ says it does not sell personal data for monetary compensation, but the site footer says 'We may sell your sensitive personal data.' Marketing email/text with opt-out. Points come from surveys and receipt scans.
notes: The former pgeveryday.com now leads to P&G brandSAVER. No baby-specific offer is listed on the rewards page. Eligibility rules are not on the pages read (see Offer Rules page).

name: Pampers Rewards
whatYouGet: Free loyalty app: scan the QR code inside Pampers diaper or wipe packs to earn Pampers Cash; the page says $10 Pampers Cash for every 10 diaper scans (most boxes have 2 scans), redeemable for discounts on Pampers at retailers.
costDetail: Free to download and join (page says no subscription or hidden fees). No sign-up gift or bonus is stated on the page; earning Pampers Cash requires buying Pampers products, and rewards are discounts on Pampers purchases.
catches: Earning needs Pampers purchases. Pampers Cash expires 6 months after being added or if the account is inactive 6 months. App works on one device at a time. Page also promotes a 7-day free trial of a separate Baby Sleep app.
notes: Formerly called Pampers Club. Page says extra bonuses at milestones and a referral: invite up to 5 friends for $2 each for them and up to $10 for you. Rate checked on pampers.com today: $10 per 10 diaper scans is what the page states.

name: Breast pumps through insurance
whatYouGet: Supplier checks your insurance, gets the prescription from your doctor and ships a covered breast pump if your plan covers one; shipping is free.
costDetail: No cost to you if your plan covers the pump; upgrades may cost extra
eligibility: People whose health plan covers a breast pump; coverage, timing and prescription rules vary by plan.
catches: Edgepark says verification is never a guarantee of coverage; out-of-pocket cost depends on your plan and deductible; some models have restricted access and plans may only ship closer to the due date.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. Search results say you can order during pregnancy and up to one year after birth, and that Edgepark works with 1,400+ plans. On 2026-11-10 the link was changed to the www address, which is the one official search results list.

name: Breastfeeding benefits (breast pump coverage)
whatYouGet: Health plans must cover the cost of a breast pump (rental or one you keep) and provide breastfeeding support, counseling and equipment, before and after birth.
costDetail: Covered by your health plan; the page does not state costs beyond this
eligibility: People with a Marketplace or other health plan, except grandfathered plans.
catches: Plans may set guidelines on manual vs. electric, rental length and timing; some require doctor pre-authorization. Grandfathered plans are exempt.
notes: How to claim (from HealthCare.gov and suppliers' own pages): 1) Contact your plan to ask about pump type (manual/electric), rental vs. purchase, timing and whether your doctor must pre-authorize. 2) Pick an in-network supplier and use its online coverage check (have your insurance card and due date ready). 3) The supplier verifies benefits and, where required, contacts your doctor for a prescription. 4) Choose a covered pump; the order ships per your plan's timing (Aeroflow notes many plans ship no sooner than 30 days before the due date). Contact your insurance plan with questions.

name: ByramBaby: Breast Pumps Through Insurance
whatYouGet: Supplier checks your insurance, handles paperwork and ships a covered breast pump if your plan covers one.
costDetail: No cost to you if your plan covers the pump; upgrades may cost extra
eligibility: People whose health plan covers a breast pump; coverage, timing and prescription rules vary by plan.
catches: An account is required to see covered pumps. Most insurers require a prescription; Byram contacts your doctor. Some pumps are partially covered (upgrade cost).
notes: Steps per Byram: 1) Select your insurance and create an account. 2) Choose a pump. 3) Place your order and Byram verifies with your insurer. 4) Pump ships (timing depends on insurance; page says within 4-5 days of order or of the due date window). Have your prescription and insurance card ready. byramhealthcare.com redirects to byrambaby.com.

name: Health coverage if you're pregnant
whatYouGet: Explains that all Marketplace and Medicaid plans cover pregnancy and childbirth, and how to apply (create an account for Marketplace coverage, or check Medicaid/CHIP eligibility) or report a pregnancy or birth.
costDetail: Free to apply; Medicaid/CHIP coverage is free or low-cost; Marketplace plans may have premiums.
eligibility: People who are pregnant or recently gave birth; Medicaid/CHIP depends on state and income.
catches: Pregnancy alone does not open a Special Enrollment Period; the birth of a child does (apply within 60 days of birth). Open Enrollment runs Nov 1 - Jan 15. Marketplace plans can have premiums, deductibles and copays.
notes: Medicaid or CHIP coverage can begin any time if you are eligible.

name: Insurance-Covered Breast Pumps
whatYouGet: Supplier checks your insurance, handles paperwork and ships a covered breast pump if your plan covers one.
costDetail: No cost to you if your plan covers the pump; upgrades may cost extra
eligibility: People whose health plan covers a breast pump; coverage, timing and prescription rules vary by plan.
catches: Site says most moms are fully covered; shipping follows insurance guidelines, so start the check around week 20. Breast pumps cannot be returned or exchanged once shipped. If your plan is not covered, the site offers 20% off retail instead. Other paid products (e.g. gender test, $169) are separate.
notes: Steps per 1NW: 1) Check coverage (about 2 minutes). 2) Choose a covered pump and accessories. 3) Pump ships free, timed to your insurance guidelines. Sign-up page is /register.

name: Lactation support covered by insurance
whatYouGet: Insurance-covered lactation consultations with an IBCLC, in-home, in-office or online.
costDetail: Page says care is covered by insurance where your plan is eligible; the registration step confirms eligibility. Your plan's copay or deductible, if any, is not stated.
eligibility: People whose insurance covers lactation support and is in The Lactation Network's network; you provide your insurance card details at registration.
region: US (50 states and DC; insurance-network dependent)
catches: Coverage check is not a guarantee; eligibility is confirmed after you register. Babies cannot be added to insurance before birth, so baby insurance details are added after the birth.
notes: Fetched directly: home page says see an IBCLC in-home, in-office or online, all covered by insurance; Check eligibility goes to the registration form. FAQ says registration asks for demographics, email, phone and insurance card. Pump supply is not part of this offer on the pages read.

name: Medicaid & CHIP coverage (pregnancy)
whatYouGet: Free or low-cost coverage for eligible pregnant women; CHIP states can cover prenatal, delivery and postpartum care, and newborns of covered mothers are deemed eligible.
costDetail: Free or low-cost; varies by state
eligibility: Income-based (MAGI) and non-financial criteria; rules vary by state. Postpartum care is covered at least 60 days, and many states extend to 12 months.
catches: Details such as income limits differ by state.
notes: You can apply any time of year. When a pregnant woman is enrolled in Medicaid or CHIP, her newborn is automatically enrolled (InsureKidsNow.gov).

name: Qualify for a Free Breast Pump Through Insurance
whatYouGet: Supplier checks your insurance, handles paperwork and ships a covered breast pump if your plan covers one.
costDetail: No cost to you if your plan covers the pump; upgrades may cost extra
eligibility: People whose health plan covers a breast pump; coverage, timing and prescription rules vary by plan.
catches: Form asks for email, due date, name, date of birth, phone, state and insurance details; includes optional marketing opt-in. Most insurers require a prescription (Aeroflow contacts your doctor). Shipping follows insurer rules.
notes: Steps per Aeroflow: 1) Fill out the form with due date and insurance info (during pregnancy or up to one year postpartum). 2) Aeroflow verifies benefits and shows covered items. 3) Add your covered pump to the cart; Aeroflow handles the prescription and paperwork. Free shipping on covered items. Pumping Essentials (pumpingessentials.com) says it is part of the Aeroflow family and uses Aeroflow's form, terms and optional marketing opt-in, so it is covered by this entry.

whatYouGet: Confidential help finding local resources for paying bills, food, housing, utilities, healthcare and other needs: call 2-1-1 and a local expert connects you to services. National Diaper Bank Network's page also points families to 2-1-1 for diaper assistance.
costDetail: Page does not state a cost; the service is a referral line, not a benefit itself.
eligibility: Anyone.
catches: Resources and what they offer vary by local 211 service; 2-1-1 refers you to programs rather than providing items itself.
notes: Fetched directly: home page says every call is completely confidential and links to local 211 lookup. Not baby-specific.

name: Early Head Start (services for pregnant women)
whatYouGet: Early Head Start programs may serve pregnant women and expectant families.
costDetail: Free
eligibility: Generally income at or below the federal poverty level, or receiving TANF, SSI or SNAP; only programs that choose to serve pregnant women do so.
catches: Not every program serves pregnant women; waiting lists possible.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. headstart.gov returned 403 to automated fetching; official-domain search results say apply by contacting a local program (Head Start Center Locator or toll-free line 1-866-763-6481) and that waitlists are common.

name: Find a Crib
whatYouGet: Free portable crib and safe sleep education through local partners.
costDetail: Free through partner organizations
eligibility: Financial need, infant 12 months or younger, and receiving safe sleep education (per search result); each partner sets its own criteria; crib limits 30 lb and 35 in.
catches: Some partners provide education only; availability varies.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. Site returned 403 to automated fetching, so this rests on official-domain search results. Search results say you find the nearest partner on the site map and call to apply; if you are not eligible the site suggests Healthy Start or local health departments.

name: Get a Car Seat Checked
whatYouGet: Free car seat inspection events and a search for certified child passenger safety technicians who check installation and teach you to install it yourself.
costDetail: Safe Kids coalitions host 8,000+ free inspection events
eligibility: Anyone with a child car seat.
catches: Inspection and education only; not a free car seat. The page says events are free but does not say whether individual technicians or inspection stations charge. Availability depends on local events and technicians.
notes: Fetched directly: page says Safe Kids coalitions host more than 8,000 free car seat inspection events and lists three ways to find a certified technician (events, the technician search, NHTSA's directory). Bring the car seat and vehicle manuals; you install the seat yourself with guidance.

name: Get Help Now / Member Diaper Banks
whatYouGet: Directs families to local diaper assistance via 2-1-1 and a directory of member diaper banks that distribute free diapers.
costDetail: Free diapers from local diaper banks
eligibility: Families in need; each local program sets its own rules.
catches: Availability varies by community; NDBN does not distribute diapers directly.
notes: Fetched directly. Per the page: call 2-1-1 or search 211.org for diapers or basic needs, check listings under children, try faith-based groups and food pantries, or use the member diaper bank directory at /member-directory/.

name: Healthy Start
whatYouGet: Community projects offering care coordination, education and support before, during and after pregnancy.
costDetail: Free through local projects
eligibility: Pregnant women, new parents, children to 18 months and partners in a funded service area.
catches: Only in funded communities.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. hrsa.gov and mchb.hrsa.gov returned 403; official-domain search results say projects have different enrollment guidelines, you must live in a served area, and the HRSA page lists a site finder.

name: PSI HelpLine
whatYouGet: Free, confidential helpline for perinatal mental health support and resources; call or text 800-944-4773 (Spanish text 971-203-7773), leave a message and a trained volunteer returns your call or text.
costDetail: Free and confidential
eligibility: Anyone; no diagnosis needed.
catches: Not for emergencies; response times vary (search results cite business-hours return, and up to about 48 hours on the Spanish page).
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. postpartum.net returned 403 to automated fetching; details from official-domain search results. In crisis call or text 988.

name: WIC (Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children)
whatYouGet: Healthy foods, nutrition education, breastfeeding support and referrals for pregnant, postpartum and breastfeeding women, infants and children under 5.
costDetail: Foods provided at no cost; apply through a local WIC agency
eligibility: Women who are pregnant, postpartum (up to 6 months after pregnancy ends) or breastfeeding (up to the infant's first birthday), infants, and children under 5; income at or below WIC limits (or on Medicaid, SNAP or TANF), live in the state, and complete a free health check.
region: US (apply through your state or local WIC agency)
catches: Requires an appointment with a local WIC agency; bring ID, proof of address and proof of income or program enrollment as the agency instructs.
notes: Steps: 1) Use the Eligibility Tool. 2) Contact your local WIC agency by phone or online to start. 3) Attend an in-person or virtual appointment. fns.usda.gov now redirects to fna.usda.gov (Food and Nutrition Administration).

name: BzzAgent
whatYouGet: Community that invites members by email to apply for free product samples from brands, then share an honest review per posting instructions.
costDetail: Participation is free; members are not paid for reviews
eligibility: Must be 18+ (or the age of majority where you live); the platform is operated in the United States.
catches: The join link on bzzagent.com goes to sampling.powerreviews.com, which is off the bzzagent.com domain (PowerReviews owns BzzAgent). Samples are limited and only chosen applicants get one. Required review and posting per campaign, shared with followers, with disclosure rules. Sponsoring brands may receive info about your participation and act as independent controllers. Privacy notice says it does not sell data for money but shares data with ad/analytics partners, which may count as a sale or share under state law. Campaign invite emails.
notes: Not parenting-specific. Confidence capped at medium because the sign-up step is on another domain.

name: Home Tester Club
whatYouGet: Free to join. Members can apply for free product tests with samples mailed to them, then rate and review them; points are earned for activity. Current campaigns have included children's oral care products.
costDetail: Completely free to join
eligibility: Product tests are matched to member profile; not everyone is selected
catches: Not every applicant gets a test. Test partner companies can see your survey answers, written reviews with first name, and photo/video reviews, tied to profile demographics (name, email, phone and address are not shared with them per the policy). Feedback surveys and email after tests. Points have no monetary value.
notes: Not parenting-specific; check the Test page for baby or kids' campaigns.

name: Influenster VoxBox
whatYouGet: Selected members may receive free product boxes (VoxBoxes) to try and review; has a New Parent product category. Not guaranteed.
costDetail: Free to join; boxes go to selected members only
eligibility: Terms bar anyone under 16 from using the service
catches: Official guide (via search results) says to be eligible for a VoxBox you must sign up and download the app. Not guaranteed a VoxBox; selection depends on activity and impact score. Recipients are expected to post reviews or social content and disclose the product was free. Privacy policy: shares name/last initial/location with third parties who may publish it, shares aggregate data with advertisers, and shares data with partners and service providers; reviews and profile are public. Marketing about specials and new features by email.
notes: Checked from the official site's search results; the site blocks automated reading, so details may be incomplete. Home page and article pages returned a Cloudflare bot challenge (403), so offer details rest on official-domain search results. Privacy policy and terms pages were read. Not parenting-specific.

name: PINCHme
whatYouGet: Apply for free product samples; once qualified for 4 products your box ships free. Feedback on samples unlocks more offers, and extra surveys can earn gift cards.
costDetail: Free to join, no credit card required, box ships free at 4 products
catches: Terms say members are not guaranteed any samples. Privacy policy says information is shared with affiliates, business partners and brand partners for their own business purposes, including direct marketing. Marketing emails about campaigns and offers. Members are asked to share feedback and must follow FTC endorsement disclosure rules.
notes: Not parenting-specific. Terms say membership may be limited by territory and eligibility; the specific rules were not found on the pages read.

name: Tryazon
whatYouGet: Members apply to host parties or receive TryaBoxes of brand products to try, with promised free products per the site.
costDetail: Described as free to try and keep products; sponsor selects participants
eligibility: 18+ (per Terms of Use); US and Canada applicants accepted; sponsors select by demographics such as location, age or number of children
catches: As fetched today, the sign-up form page displayed 'forms are currently under maintenance' and the TryaBox page listed no open opportunities. Applications are shared with the sponsoring brand. FAQ says selection also looks at social accounts and who actively shares, and hosts follow FTC disclosure rules, so expect to post on social media. Privacy policy says it will not sell or rent your information and shares aggregated demographics with partners. Email communications with unsubscribe.
notes: Terms of Use page shows an effective date of May 25, 2018. Specific what-you-get varies by party or TryaBox.
